In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for aResearch associate (m/f/x)The group conducts core research in artificial intelligence and machine learning, with a primary focus on online decision-making under uncertainty. Our work spans areas such as (inverse, deep, and causal) reinforcement learning, multiarmed bandits, and learning in multi-agent systems involving cooperation, competition, and coordination. We are particularly interested in how intelligent systems can adapt across changing domains and recover from suboptimal or biased decisions through principled approaches to domain adaptation and algorithmic recourse. While our methods are generic and applicable across diverse fields—including medicine, education, and finance—we primarily apply them to engineering and technical systems, such as the Internet of Things, nextgeneration communication networks, and robotics.The researcher will work on the development of robust and efficient collective algorithmic recourse methods to enhance the resilience of mission-critical networked systems. The project lies at the intersection of machine learning, optimization, and multi-agent systems, addressing challenges arising from resource volatility and uncertainty in dynamic environments. The work will include both theoretical analysis—covering efficiency, scalability, and convergence—as well as the application of the proposed methods to optimize networked systems.Scope: full-timeDuration: fixed-term, 36 monthsStart: at the earliest possible dateApply by:  2026-11-02Your tasks:- The main task is to conduct high-quality and independent research in the area of collective algorithmic recourse, with a particular focus on its application to networked systems, and to publish the results in leading scientific venues.Your profile:- An excellent, recently completed Ph.D. or M.Sc. degree with a strong publication record in Computer Science (Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence), Mathematics (pure or applied, including Operations Research), Electrical Engineering (Signal Processing, Information Theory), or related fields such as Theoretical Physics.- A solid mathematical background.- Strong programming skills.- Excellent command of English, both written and spoken.https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/e4100af2a4b9c3fb3f09a53cd2345db05d259b970?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/e4100af2a4b9c3fb3f09a53cd2345db05d259b970?ref=AfA)

Neuronal exocytosis is a highly regulated process that enables the rapid release of neurotransmitters from synaptic vesicles. Central to this process is the controlled assembly of SNARE protein complexes, which drive membrane fusion and are regulated by a network of associated proteins. The PhD project will investigate the structural and molecular mechanisms underlying SNARE complex assembly and function in membrane-like environments. A particular focus will be placed on the development and characterization of membrane-mimetic systems, including lipid nanodiscs and synthetic copolymers, to study SNARE complexes and their regulatory proteins under increasingly native-like conditions. Cryo-electron microscopy will be combined with complementary biochemical and biophysical approaches to characterize these systems at the molecular level.The project offers the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary structural biology environment at Forschungszentrum Jülich, with access to expertise in cryo-EM, NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography. Cryo-EM studies will be conducted at the state-of-the-art facilities of the Ernst Ruska-Centre (ER-C) at Forschungszentrum Jülich. The expertise in NMR spectroscopy and macromolecular crystallography at IBI-7 offers further opportunities for complementary structural and biophysical characterization. This combination of methods will enable the candidate to address biological questions from different structural perspectives and to develop a broad expertise in modern structural biology. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:A Master’s degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, structural biology, or a related fieldStrong practical experience in protein biochemistry, including recombinant protein expression and purificationPrevious hands-on experience with cryo-electron microscopy and/or cryo-EM sample preparationInterest in membrane proteins, protein-protein interactions and structural biologyAbility to work independently as well as in an interdisciplinary research teamGood communication skills in English
